neighbours.label: the hyphen-attached opening piece of a split word inside a compound modifier (-con|tract, -fe|ver, -br|anded, -del|ivered), as opposed to the same modifiers written without a hyphen compound
fire: The engineers built a space-constrained version of the pump.
Each record in the file is a comma-delimited list of fields.
The chef keeps a store-branded olive oil for everyday cooking.
Mosquitoes spread yellow-fever outbreaks in the colonial ports.
She bought a stiff-bristled brush to scrub the patio.
The firm switched to completed-contract reporting last year.
Bring a white-feathered hat for the costume parade.
Our hotel offered a room-delivered breakfast every morning.
quiet: The engineers built a smaller version of the pump for tight spaces.
Each record in the file is a list of fields with commas between them.
The chef keeps a cheap olive oil from the store for everyday cooking.
Mosquitoes spread outbreaks of fever in the colonial ports.
She bought a stiff brush to scrub the patio.
The firm switched to reporting each contract when it finished.
Bring a white hat with feathers for the costume parade.
Our hotel brought breakfast to the room every morning.

predictions: hyphenated compounds whose second word splits as '-xx'+rest 0.4-0.75; unhyphenated paraphrases below 0.05
short: hyphen + opening piece of split compound word
